A $2 trillion debut in October would represent roughly a 2.1x step up from that Series H price in approximately five months, an extraordinarily compressed timeline for that kind of valuation jump even by the standards of this year’s AI funding boom.

ALSO READ: Anthropic’s Projected $2 Trillion IPO Track Threatens to Eclipse SpaceX Market Capitalization

## Who’s Actually Running the Deal [...] Not every voice covering this story is convinced the number holds up cleanly. A Forbes analysis framed the situation as a genuine test of whether AI valuations have entered bubble territory, noting that Anthropic’s economics differ meaningfully from traditional software companies: usage drives both revenue and substantial operating expense simultaneously, given the enormous compute costs required to actually run frontier AI models at scale. That dynamic raises real questions about sustainable [...] Would its rapid revenue growth justify a $2 trillion valuation for Anthropic, or is it another sign that AI valuations have moved too far, too fast? Stripe finalized a deal to acquire OpenRouter, the AI model routing gateway, for more than $7 billion, a 5.4x markup on the $1.3 billion valuation OpenRouter carried just three months earlier.
 The price implies roughly 50 times OpenRouter’s annualized revenue, which means Stripe paid for strategic position, not cash flow, and the position it bought is narrower and more specific than “the orchestration layer.” [...] Get a ranked list of which AI infrastructure bets are exposed to the next wave of commoditization, and which are not.
 Learn the reusable framework for spotting where value actually stops pooling in any commoditizing technology stack, not just this one.
 Walk away with specific positioning moves for founders, consultants, investors, and executives, not general commentary. [...] Understand why Stripe paid roughly 50 times revenue for a company that, on paper, was barely monetizing its own scale.
 Identify why “value moves to the layer above the commodity” is true but dangerously incomplete, and the one question that fixes it.
 See the specific, underreported fact (46% of US enterprise AI tokens routed through non-Western models) that turns this from a tech story into a policy story.
